counterfactual_missing_items: No lipid-laden foam cells or multinucleated giant cells
decisive_items: FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positive on RT-PCR
Blood cell count showed hypereosinophilia (4220/μL; reference range 50-250/μL)
Elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL; reference range <11.5 ng/mL)
response.rationale: R6 is supported by the disease-defining FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion together with hypereosinophilia, myeloid hyperplasia, elevated tryptase/vitamin B12, and eosinophil-rich tissue infiltration. R2 captures the eosinophilic syndrome but lacks the specific genetic driver, and the other candidates address only skin/histologic or tryptase features without the definitive molecular etiology.

rejected.why: Only describes eosinophilic skin lesions and hypereosinophilia; no molecular or bone marrow specificity.
Elevated tryptase alone is not specific; biopsy lacks mast cell aggregates and no mastocytosis-defining histology or mutation.
Skin histiocytic IHC is supportive of tissue infiltration but misses the hematologic/neoplastic driver; CD1a negativity also argues against Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
Generic eosinophilic disorder label is too broad and does not integrate the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion or bone marrow pathology.
